items.title: Families and police at odds over findings in Laos methanol poisoning case
items.description: The families of six people, including two Australians, who died from suspected mass methanol poisoning at a Laos hostel have described the outcome of a 20-month police investigation into the incident as "false".

items.title: Legacy stores have been closing but physical retail is not 'dead'
items.description: It has been a brutal year for Australian retail, with high rents, wage increases and the cost-of-living squeeze forcing big brands to make some hard calls. Here's why some are still surviving.

items.title: Clean energy investment is facing headwinds. Could superannuation help?
items.description: Australian super funds manage $4.5 trillion in retirement savings, but directing some of that war chest towards the clean energy transition could be more difficult than it seems.

items.title: What Labor gains and loses by hiding its fights
items.description: If Labor has a policy fight behind a closed door and nobody else hears, did it really happen?

items.title: We asked what you wanted to talk about most. Here's what you told us
items.description: Thousands of Australians have shared their stories, concerns and hopes for the future. Here's what matters most to you.

items.title: Prince William's 'manifesto' for the king he will become
items.description: As heir to the throne William was born into singular privilege. How he uses it and the work he chooses to pursue presents a 'manifesto' for the king he will become.

items.title: Live: Godwin puts gymnasts on brink of gold, Aussies score first podium sweep
items.description: Australia's swimmers will look to continue their day one gold rush as finals begin in the pool on day two of the Commonwealth Games. Follow live.

items.title: Two people shot by police during altercation in Cairns
items.description: Police say a woman and a man have been shot in Cairns during an altercation with an armed suspect.

items.title: Hopes excavations in northern France can shed light on diggers' sacrifice
items.description: On the edge of a tiny village in northern France, a team of archaeologists are digging through ground that was fought for, and won, by the sacrifice of Australian soldiers.

items.title: How two boats with 500 people disappeared almost without trace
items.description: The disappearance of two boats carrying more than 500 Rohingya asylum seekers off the coast of Myanmar in recent weeks brings the number of people reported lost at sea in the region this year to more than 800.

items.title: Indian education minister resigns after Cockroach movement protests
items.description: Protesters had been calling for Dharmandra Pradhan's resignation amid ongoing exam paper leaks, which the education minister claims he "took responsibility" for.

items.title: Attack on holiday camp in Russian-held Ukraine kills 11
items.description: Moscow-installed officials say Ukrainian forces attacked holiday camps in the partly Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia region overnight, killing 11 people and wounding 14.

items.title: Fires claim lives in France and Spain, forcing 250,000 people to flee their homes
items.description: An entire peninsula in the south of France has been evacuated, while in Spain, the government has declared a national emergency as fires encroach on the capital Madrid.

items.title: Houthis and Saudi Arabia trade fire amid Red Sea blockade
items.description: Houthi rebels have claimed missile attacks on Saudia Arabia's cities of Jazan and Yanbu, after Riyadh struck military targets in Yemen following the Iran-backed group's Red Sea blockade.

items.title: For Beth Orton, the messiness of being human has never sounded better
items.description: At 55, the British musician navigates aging, loss and loving imperfectly in ways she never could as the 90s queen of folktronica.

items.title: Want a music quiz? You should be so lucky (lucky, lucky, lucky)
items.description: This is the Spicks and Specks quiz, where your many years of rage viewing are rewarded.

items.title: The 10 books our critics couldn't put down in July
items.description: This month's best new books include an erotic novel set in a Tasmanian lighthouse, a 'wonderfully weird debut' about a woman's obsession with a cat and a Harlem heist novel.

items.title: Fifty years of weather records help farmers plan ahead
items.description: Fifty years of weather data is helping western Queensland graziers adapt to hotter conditions by changing breeding schedules and improving livestock survival.

items.title: Mandarin and orange supply down in SA amid extreme weather
items.description: Shoppers may see fewer oranges and mandarins from South Australia's Riverland on their shelves amid record-breaking heatwaves and wetter, colder winter days.

items.title: Trump mixes jokes with barbs at press freedom dinner
items.description: US President Donald Trump has poked fun at the press during a redo of the White House Correspondents' Association dinner after a shooting forced the suspension of the original event in April.

items.title: Iran's attacks on US bases in the Middle East mark 'end of an era'
items.description: Five months into a war Donald Trump said would last only weeks, the Iran conflict has so far cost the United States tens of billions of dollars and brought about "the end of an era" in American military strategy.

items.title: Dogs too strong for Tigers, Hawks and Swans dominate
items.description: The Western Bulldogs ease past a determined young Richmond side for a 57-point win after Hawthorn and Sydney record big wins of their own.

items.title: Brisbane's premiership defence all but over after Cowboys crash-out
items.description: Brisbane's tumultuous premiership defence is over in all but name after the Broncos fell to the Cowboys in a blood and thunder Queensland derby.

items.title: An addiction started at school landed Clay in a maximum-security prison
items.description: Clay first tried drugs during lunchtime at school. What followed was a decade of addiction and run-ins with police. Now he hopes sharing his story will help others.

items.title: Drivers urged to play their part as five people die on WA roads in 24 hours
items.description: Five people have been killed in separate crashes in Western Australia in less than 24 hours, as the state's road toll continues to soar.
